clue.text: Spiritualist aimed to reverse position

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: at a seance, spiritualists set out to make the furniture rotate
second meaning: to swap places with an opponent so the one who was losing now wins

explanation.surface: A medium sets out to make a dramatic switch of sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Victorian table-turning was a seance trick in which a table moved under the sitters' hands; the idiom TURN THE TABLES has nothing to do with seances.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reverse a situation so the former underdog gains the advantage over a rival.

clue.text: Damaged, so better suit not to be used?

definitions.text: so better suit not to be used?

blocks.note: first meaning: worn and in poor condition

blocks.clueFragment: so better suit not to be used?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: the inferior outfit is the one for everyday wearing, so the good one is kept

explanation.surface: A spoilt garment means the good suit stays in the wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase literally: the worse suit is the one for wear, which spares the better one.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something or someone showing deterioration from use, tiredness or drink.

clue.text: In the height of fashion, new line of merchandise

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, so a letter is placed within a word

blocks.note: the rage is the current craze
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A new product line that is ultra-fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a set of related products offered by one maker or retailer.

clue.text: American native in wood cooked turtle pie

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters of the dish are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Native American in the forest cooks a turtle pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American native' suggests a person; it is a tree native to North America, found in woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip tree is a tall North American magnolia relative with tulip-shaped flowers, valued for timber.

clue.text: Get person to box, when decision on points is needed

definitions.text: Get person to box, when decision on points is needed

blocks.clueFragment: Get person to box, when decision on points is needed
blocks.note: surface reading: putting someone in the ring for a fight judged on points
setter's reading: enrol someone for the jury box, where a verdict on the points of a case is required

explanation.surface: A fighter is sent into the ring for a bout decided by the judges' scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' means fight and 'points' suggest scoring, but the box is the jury box and the points are those argued in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To empanel is to enrol people on a jury list, so they sit in judgment on a case.

clue.text: Heights of Peruvian desolation?

indicators.note: 'of' marks the answer as made out of the following words, sitting inside their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Peru's lonely mountain wastes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition fits the surface too, since these mountains run through Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American mountain range is the longest continental chain on earth, spanning several countries.

clue.text: Is one in order to preach? Yes and no

definitions.text: Is one in order to preach? Yes and no

blocks.clueFragment: Is one in order to preach?
blocks.note: surface reading: whether it is permissible for someone to give a sermon
setter's reading: this person is allowed to preach but is not in holy orders

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is acceptable to give a sermon, and gets an equivocal reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order' means permitted, and also ordained in holy orders; this church officer is licensed but not ordained.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay reader is a layman licensed by the Anglican church to conduct services and preach without being a priest.

clue.text: Go through formalities to accept pound note, changing money

indicators.note: changing money, as at a bureau, here means altering the order of its letters

blocks.note: to stand something is to put up with it
a oncer was old British slang for a one-pound note
taken as written

explanation.surface: Doing the official paperwork to take a banknote at a bureau de change.
explanation.walkthrough: A oncer is a one-pound note, withdrawn from circulation in England in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand on ceremony is to insist on correct, formal behaviour and etiquette.

clue.text: Head's drug-taking veto

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: a veto is a prohibition
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A headteacher bans drug-taking at the school.
explanation.definitionFit: Bean is informal slang for a person's skull or brain, as in 'use your bean'.

clue.text: Easy to understand where mass has been lost in body fat

indicators.note: something lost is no longer present, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: limpid prose is clear and lucid
M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A simple explanation of how weight is lost from body fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M out of LIMPID to leave LIPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipids are the biochemical class of fats and oils stored in living tissue.

clue.text: Set of school classes in revolutionary period

blocks.note: first meaning: all the pupils of one age group, as in the third ___
second meaning: the time the earth takes for one orbit of the sun

explanation.surface: A group of school classes studying a period of revolution in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests political upheaval, but here it is the earth revolving round the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A school intake is grouped by age cohort, and one orbit of the sun takes twelve months.

clue.text: Unsophisticated detective's left missing joke

indicators.note: missing means absent, so that abbreviation is dropped from the detective's name

blocks.note: Sherlock Holmes, the fictional detective
L is the abbreviation for left
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A naive sleuth fails to get the joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'left missing joke' as one phrase; 'left missing' is the deletion instruction and 'joke' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun originally described cloth woven at home, hence plain, simple and lacking refinement.

clue.text: Girl-friend coming in ready to go

definitions.note: the word that comes between 'ready' and 'go' in the starting call

blocks.note: first meaning: a regular romantic partner
second meaning: the word that sits between ready and go in a race starter's call

explanation.surface: A girlfriend arrives, all set to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The starter's call is 'Ready, steady, go!', so the answer literally comes in the middle of 'ready ... go'.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, and the word also completes the familiar race-starting phrase.

clue.text: Recess over, mostly bored, put one's foot in it

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read from end to start
mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: an apse is a semicircular recess in a church
to bore a hole is to drill it

explanation.surface: Break-time is finished, and a bored person makes a social blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot in it' looks like the idiom for a gaffe, but it describes a shoe: an ESPADRILLE is a rope-soled canvas shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe is literally something you place your foot inside, so the idiom becomes a playful description of footwear.

clue.text: Water spirit losing footing in a marsh that's overflowing

indicators.note: in a down entry the foot is the bottom, i.e. the last letter, which is dropped
in places the shortened spirit inside the marsh phrase

blocks.note: taken as written
a bog is a marsh
an undine is a female water sprite

explanation.surface: A water nymph slips while wading through a flooded swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the 'foot' of a word is its last letter, since the word stands upright in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abounding is present in great quantity, teeming or brimming over.

clue.text: Vital troops protecting one line in support of German city

indicators.note: soldiers protecting something surround it, so the troops wrap around the numeral
in a down clue support sits underneath, so these letters follow the city's name

blocks.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr
TA is the Territorial Army
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Soldiers guarding a vital supply line to a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve; Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential means absolutely necessary, something that cannot be done without.

clue.text: Eat noisily, with a measure of force

indicators.note: doing it noisily means it is heard, so we want a word that sounds the same

blocks.note: to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone eats loudly and forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: The dyne is the old CGS unit of force, equal to one hundred-thousandth of a newton.

clue.text: Shaped hairstyle, for a change

indicators.note: for a change suggests variety, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Trying out a new hairstyle for a change.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy hairstyle of tightly curled hair, cut and combed into shape.

clue.text: Being well off the roadway, child's play takes precedence

definitions.note: the answer is the state of affluence, as in 'on easy street'

indicators.note: taking precedence means going first, so this piece is placed before the other

blocks.note: child's play is something very simple
a street is a road

explanation.surface: Children's games should come first, away from the traffic on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well off the roadway' reads as safely away from traffic; in fact 'well off' means wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Living on easy street is an idiom for enjoying comfortable prosperity without money worries.

clue.text: Mounting scaffold

blocks.note: first meaning: putting on a play
second meaning: a temporary platform of planks and poles

explanation.surface: Climbing up a gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounting scaffold' reads like ascending to an execution; both words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre production is put on stage, and builders' temporary platforms are also called by this name.

clue.text: Emotional tug of leaving St Paul's, say?

blocks.note: first meaning: the painful pang of departure
second meaning, split as two words: a church designed by Christopher Wren, with CH the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: The sadness of departing from St Paul's Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: St Paul's Cathedral in London was designed by Sir Christopher Wren, so it is a WREN CH(urch); the question mark flags the punning split.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a sudden painful feeling of separation, especially when parting from a person or place.

clue.text: Throw hard over part of roof? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is cut
in a down clue over means above, so the abbreviation is placed first

blocks.note: H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard
the eaves are the overhanging lower edge of a roof

explanation.surface: Someone hurls something forcefully over the roof edge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts H above the rest; EAVES loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to lift and fling something heavy with great effort.

clue.text: Mass movement gained us representation

indicators.note: re-presentation means setting out again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A popular mass campaign has won people like us political representation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass movement' suggests popular politics, but it is a section of the Catholic Mass set to music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei is a part of the Mass liturgy and a standard section in musical settings of it.

clue.text: Part of barrel taverner's opening in bar

indicators.note: an opening is the very start, so only the innkeeper's initial is used
in means placed inside, so that letter goes within the other word

blocks.note: bar and save both mean except, as in 'all bar one'
the innkeeper's initial letter

explanation.surface: A cask in a pub cellar, opened by the landlord at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, which suits the barrel and the taverner, but it means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A stave is one of the curved wooden strips that form the sides of a barrel.

clue.text: Mysterious creature of very great height

definitions.text: Mysterious creature of very great height

blocks.clueFragment: Mysterious creature of very great height
blocks.note: surface reading: an enigmatic giant of a beast
setter's reading: the beast belongs to the high mountains, living among Himalayan peaks

explanation.surface: An unexplained, gigantic animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of very great height' sounds like the creature is tall; it means it lives at altitude in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman is a legendary ape-like beast said to roam the high snows of the Himalayas.

clue.text: Claim that one was seen off the premises

definitions.text: Claim that one was seen off the premises

blocks.note: surface reading: someone being escorted or thrown out of a building

blocks.clueFragment: Claim that one was seen off the premises
blocks.note: setter's reading: a defence that the accused was observed elsewhere at the time of the crime

explanation.surface: Someone insists they were ejected from the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen off' suggests being chased away, but it means spotted somewhere other than the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a suspect's plea of having been somewhere else when the offence took place.

clue.text: Bitter taste from this beer, having collected round

indicators.note: having collected something means holding it, so the drink wraps around the circle

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A bitter flavour comes from this beer, after a round has been bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' and 'round' suggest a pub, but the definition points to a plant whose sap is famously bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice of the aloe plant is notoriously harsh-flavoured, and 'bitter aloes' was a traditional purgative medicine.

clue.text: Crook goes regularly into these police files

blocks.note: surface reading: a criminal repeatedly entering some place
setter's reading: a habitual offender's mugshot keeps being added to the police photo collection

explanation.surface: A criminal keeps turning up in police records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes regularly into' sounds like visiting a gallery; a repeat offender's photo is filed there each time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the police collection of photographs of known criminals, used for identification by witnesses.
